Visual Design.assessment:
# Cycle 45 — Visual Design Reviewer

**REVISE.** The certification values stay beside their labels in RTL, including after refresh. The existing right-edge mask now covers the trailing letters of every right-aligned pinned header during RTL panning. The visible regression concerns the labels themselves.

## Independent inspection

I opened the frozen port 47854 build in a fresh Chrome process after recording cycle 44. I repeated the accepted port 47851 comparison at 390×844, 900×900 and 1440×900 in light and pure-black dark modes. I inspected all six table and six context comparison sheets in `design-evidence/refresh-repair/cycle-45/` and made fresh captures in `/tmp/quartz-refresh-repair/visual-47854/`. States included the Home table’s start, midpoint and end in both directions, single and rapid reloads, phone Explorer, the Blog listing, keyboard-selected Azure search result, Linux disk article table, Azure prose and code, local and modal graphs, Escape and a live reduced-motion change. I also set RTL in the original HTML before scripts ran and repeated a phone reload from the middle and end.

## Findings

- **Material, pinned-header legibility.** Compare `visual-47854/390-dark-rtl-0.png` against `390-dark-rtl-1.png`. “Todo” goes from fully readable to two strong letters and a nearly invisible ending. “In Progress” and “Obtained” similarly lose their ends. On an otherwise solid stroke near the right of the final “o”, the captured ink changed from #f5f5f5 to #303030 against #000000 (about 1.6:1); in light mode the same stroke changed from near-black to approximately #cdcdcd on #faf9f5. It occurs at the halfway and far positions where the physical-right overflow hint is active. The cycle 44 RTL “Todo” sat farther left in its header and remained readable there. Keeping the fade off the pinned RTL Home header would resolve the interference. This is a demonstrated degradation of the table’s labels.
- **RTL fix verified.** CAISP and the dash were visible in all six viewport/theme combinations at both ends and the midpoint. With RTL applied in the source HTML, ordinary reloads retained −215px and −430px at half and full scroll in the 390px pointer configuration I tested. CAISP stayed 5px from its label. Disabling site JavaScript kept it visible with the 6.5em fallback. LTR retained 418px, 128px and 97px after single and rapid refreshes.
- **Minor paint detail.** The occasional one-pixel discontinuity below the phone’s sticky label after LTR scroll restoration occurred in one of six paired captures. It affected a rule under the label. All words remained legible.
- **Graph and motion.** In ordinary desktop Chrome and with WebGL disabled, every entry and ordinary/rapid reload yielded a local canvas, and each dialog opened to an active global canvas. The fallback graph used the theme palette. The wider trigger regained focus after Escape. Graphs were suppressed on phone; an initial reduced-motion desktop had zero canvases and the visible graph was removed when that preference changed.
- **Visual surroundings.** Source Serif 4 article prose, SN Pro 14px table text and TX-02 at 14.5px/22px held across widths. The selected search result, Explorer, archive rows, code surface and Linux table preserved their spacing and hierarchy. The ordinary Linux table pixels matched the baseline at 900px and 1440px. At phone width differences stayed within the 28px fade at the far edge. Theme surfaces measured #faf9f5 and #000000. The wide Home reading column and its neighboring graph retained their positions, and Home had no horizontal page overflow.
- **Change scope.** `quartz/styles/custom.scss` now applies logical start alignment and supplies a measured-offset fallback. `quartz/components/scripts/scrollableTables.inline.ts` handles fractional endpoints and physical-right distance. `content/index.md` supplies two spans so the short values can stay put while credentials pan. These changes fit the existing table owner rules. Pinned-header paint is the sole material issue I found.

Responsive and Accessibility.assessment:
# Cycle 45 · Responsive and Accessibility Reviewer

**REVISE.** The original short-status reading and reload defects are fixed at the tested sizes, in both directions. Two observed RTL issues affect the Home table.

- **Medium, row headings.** At 390px in RTL, pan halfway and leave focus outside the table. The physical-right edge fade overlays the pinned headings. On the accepted build the remaining ink in “Obtained” and “Todo” was clear. In the corrected build the new start alignment places their last letters against the transparent edge as well. “In Progress” is affected in both builds. The crop shows a visibly faded “Todo” and missing ends of “In Progress” and “Obtained”. Correcting the Home-specific RTL mask can preserve readable headings. Evidence in `access-rtl-mask-47851.png` and `access-rtl-mask-47854.png`.
- **Medium, pre-existing RTL keyboard focus.** Chrome lays out the final AZ-900 external icon and label as separate bidirectional fragments. Tabbing forward from the first certificate can display all ten labels. On reverse traversal at 390px, Shift+Tab from below the table focuses AZ-900 while its actual text occupies x658–707 outside the x18–360 scrollport. I reproduced this from initial scroll fractions 0, 0.5 and 1. At 900px its label was partially or wholly clipped depending on the starting position. The link exists and remains operable, but a reader cannot see what has focus. The accepted build also exhibits the issue. An isolated direction context around each Latin certificate link is worth testing. Evidence in `47854-access-rtlkeys.json`, which measures the text node and hit-tests its center independently of the icon.
- **Short values and scroll restoration.** In light and pure-black dark, CAISP and the Todo dash stay visible with JavaScript at all three panning positions. Ordinary reload and rapid double reload restore the end and midpoint. Measured LTR pairs were 430/215px, 128/64px and 97/49px. RTL pairs were −430/−215px, −128/−64px and −97/−48px. With JavaScript disabled I verified both values at all three positions in both directions and all three widths.
- **Readability, zoom and focus.** I compared all six paired Home sheets and six context sheets in `design-evidence/refresh-repair/cycle-45/` and interacted with the frozen builds in Chrome at 390×844, 900×900 and 1440×900. No page-wide horizontal overflow occurred. Native Firefox 100%, 200% and 400% zoom produced viewports of 1280, 640 and 320 CSS pixels. All status values stayed visible at the beginning, middle and end in both themes. With Chrome font sizes enlarged on the running page, table type rose from 14 to 21 and 28px and returned to 14px. The status inset rose from 82.6 to 124.4 and 166.2px and returned. All ten LTR keyboard link outlines stayed within the scrollport in both directions, and a separate forced-colors pass showed the focused label with a 2px system-colored outline.
- **Typography and contrast.** The table uses SN Pro 14px and underlined credential links, the article uses Source Serif 4 and fenced code uses TX-02 14.5px. Measured table text contrast is 17.50:1 on the light page and 19.26:1 on black, with corresponding focus-outline contrast of 13.00:1 and 15.61:1. The RTL gradient alters this locally at the inline end of the headers.
- **Surroundings and interaction.** I tested Home, the Blog listing, Linux disk article table, Azure article code, SPA navigation, mobile Explorer, keyboard Search selection/Escape and both graph modes. Search and Explorer returned focus to their openers. Graph dialog Close received focus, Tab was contained and Escape restored the trigger. Reduced motion hid local/global controls and removed both canvases, with focus on the site title when the open graph disappeared. Removing the preference restored a single local canvas. The phone had zero graph canvases.
- **Maintainability.** The logical alignment and scalable CSS fallback reuse the existing table rule. The shared physical-right mask fails to account for a sticky header on that physical edge. The observed defects warrant a narrow change to Home; I found no need for a global table redesign.

Independent browser measurements and crops are under `/tmp/quartz-refresh-repair/`, including `final-access.json`, `47854-access-nojs.json`, `47854-access-nojs-rtl.json`, `47854-access-native-zoom.json`, `47854-access-motion.json` and `47854-access-rtlkeys.json`.

CSS and Quartz V5.assessment:
# Cycle 45 · CSS and Quartz V5 review

**Decision: REVISE.** The three issues from the first review were corrected. A further pixel comparison shows that the right-edge fade clips the pinned RTL header ink, including two headers that had more clearance in the baseline.

## Coverage

Independently inspected the final paired table and context sheets in `design-evidence/refresh-repair/final` and exercised the frozen build at port 47854. Compared with the baseline on port 47851. Google Chrome 158, 390 × 844, 900 × 900 and 1440 × 900, light and pure-black dark, six complete runs without harness errors. Used Home, nine-row Linux disk-space article table, Azure Machine Configuration article code, Blog listing, keyboard-operated Azure search, Explorer and SPA navigation. Tested fractional zoom, RTL, keyboard focus in both directions, disabled JavaScript, ordinary and double refresh, local and global graph open/close, interrupted initialization, and live reduced motion.

## Confirmed changes and behavior

- Home scope, logical text alignment, a font-relative premeasurement fallback, and one measured custom property keep CAISP and the placeholder visible at all LTR and RTL offsets. Header/value gaps were 5–6 CSS px on phone and 9–10 px on wider viewports in both directions. The fallback also kept both values visible at start, middle and end with JS disabled. Computed scales, colors, SN Pro table type, 14.5 px TX-02, article/table layout, search options and navigation agreed with baseline.
- Ordinary and rapid double reloads in both themes restored 430, 128 and 97 px in the three live configurations. At 125% zoom and 1.25 device scale, the saved sentinel was 1 and the actual 508.7999878 px endpoint was restored. The measured label and hidden-distance computations use layout-pixel coordinates consistently.
- Overlapping global close/reopen left one local and one global 160-node renderer while open, then one local renderer, one ticker and one simulation after dismissal. The interrupted instance was disposed and the page recorded zero Pixi errors, versus two in cycle 44. Escape and Close returned focus to the trigger. Motion changes settled at zero then one local canvas, and the phone stayed at zero. The independent stress capture is `/tmp/quartz-refresh-repair/graph-qa/chrome-47854-css-final.json`.
- The Quartz registry keeps the upstream component markup/config, site graph JS is registered once, and resource cleanup is seen on nav/render, motion, theme and dialog transitions. The vendored renderer is accompanied by its upstream commit and MIT license. The application destructor's explicit view-only options preserve Pixi resources shared between renderers. Styling stays in the established custom SCSS, without extra theme declarations. Build and 167 tests passed. The baseline and revised full type-check logs report the same micromorph and remark-parse declarations.

## Material defect requiring revision

At 390 px, apply RTL and pan to the physical left endpoint; the scrollable table's full-width physical right-edge mask fades the visible pinned row headings. The short headings now finish at the scroller's right edge, aligning the ends of *Obtained* and *Todo* with near-transparent pixels. Compare `/tmp/quartz-refresh-repair/css-rtl-mask-47854-with.png` against the same viewport with only the mask disabled, `css-rtl-mask-47854-without.png`. The baseline `css-rtl-mask-47851-with.png` leaves more room for those two shorter labels. Sampled the final 30 px of the Todo row: 34 originally dark ink pixels became lighter than 150/255; no Todo ink fell in this area on the baseline. At the affected offset, physical right-edge fade width is 28 px. Keep the cue clear of the pinned logical-start column in RTL. An ordinary DOM hit test misses this because a CSS mask changes ink opacity.

## Existing observation

On keyboard traversal in a 390 px RTL document, the tenth link AZ-900 splits into two bidirectional inline fragments. Browser focus pans to the external icon at x23 while text remains at x658 outside the 343 px scroller. Verified identical geometry on baseline and revised builds. The changed row-level focus exception preserved LTR Tab and Shift+Tab behavior. This existing RTL link issue is distinct from the newly worsened visible header fade.

designDirector.assessment:
## Cycle 45 · REVISE

All three reviewers voted REVISE. Logical alignment and the fallback made the short statuses readable through scrolling in both directions. Fractional restoration, Pixi close/reopen and the test fixture diagnostic were corrected. The full-table mask now faded the ends of all three pinned headers in RTL at middle and far positions, with formerly readable letters of Todo and Obtained losing contrast. The final AZ-900 link could receive reverse keyboard focus with its visible label outside the scrollport. This keyboard behavior also existed in the baseline. It affects the same scrolling row, so address it in this repair. Preserve the overflow hint on exposed credentials, protect header ink and keep each external-link icon together with its link text. The divider observation remains cosmetic.
